english: In this world, suppose a father’s son is told in abundance of ordinary wealth, many possessions well known to others, and all manner of profound things. As the saying goes, “Nothing is spoken of without experiential acquaintance.” Even after gaining exceptional certainty through the four valid cognitions, whoever wastes it becomes an object of others’ reproach.[^N-C-105]

notes.problem: The wealth metaphor, saying about experiential acquaintance, and four valid cognitions are joined in a compressed construction. ཟབ་དགུ may be idiomatic all profound things rather than the numeral nine.
notes.treatment: Preserve each component and provisionally read all manner of profound things; do not invent a missing transition.
notes.uncertainty: The exact object wasted and the force of the saying require review.
notes.review_action: Review the full opening comparison U04416–U04423 against a witness.

english: How much more would one be reproached for refusing to preserve one’s father’s still more precious, exceptional wealth: kinds of jewels possessed by no one else, previously unheard of by anyone!

The comparison applies in the same way: the peerless Dharma king, protector of the three worlds, was born and actualized all meanings. These distinctive teachings, previously unheard of in this Land of Snow, were later made clear in this way by Jikten Gönpo. For his sons and followers not to preserve them is just like the case described.[^N-C-106]

notes.problem: The instrumental ending before was born is awkward; the source may intend the arising of the teacher or of his distinctive teachings.
notes.treatment: Provisionally take the Dharma king as born and as actualizing meanings; retain the later explicit Jikten Gönpo attribution.
notes.uncertainty: The attachment of the birth clause remains open.
notes.review_action: Check the case ending and full comparison.

english: Therefore, those with sound reasoning who wish to continue their father’s lineage should follow the lord’s words: “Do not disparage anyone’s Dharma. By disparaging none, there is no precipice arising through Dharma. Do not follow anyone’s Dharma. By following none, no fault of entering a mistaken course arises.”

Without indiscriminately disparaging others’ tenets or persons, [one should preserve] the distinctive teachings that are the enlightened intent accepted by Chöjé Rinpoche, Dharma king of the three realms, renowned throughout the three kinds of existence. They are the heart of all the teachings of the buddhas of the three times. A sūtra says:[^N-C-107]

notes.problem: The instruction’s main preserving verb comes after the quotation; རིགས་འཆོལ is idiomatic, and the compound ཐུགས་དགོངས contains the protected enlightened-intent family.
notes.treatment: Supply [one should preserve] from U04449, render indiscriminately provisionally, and retain enlightened intent rather than reducing it to mind.
notes.uncertainty: The precise adverbial scope and title attachment need review.
notes.review_action: Confirm the long modifier chain and the supplied verb.

english:
Even after crossing masses of fire and razor edges,
I shall uphold it to the furthest limit of the future.
As stated, if one were to uphold these with great assiduity, it would be exceedingly wondrous.

The noble people who undertake the Dharma work of upholding the teaching are like a qualified prince born into a universal monarch’s family amid a thousand sons of ordinary subjects: just as he surpasses them through many qualities, these people are beautiful with many qualities and superior among all who have entered the teaching.

What makes them superior? They are not bewildered about the uncommon Ground, the sublime Sugata heart, or the limitless stages of the path of methods that actualize it—all the Sage’s teachings. Alternatively, they are not bewildered about emptiness, Mahamudra beyond all dual phenomena, and all the dependent arising of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa in which it occurs as cause and result. Therefore, like a snow lion, they have not a hair’s breadth of fear or anxiety before the packs of jackals that are hostile outside disputants.[^N-C-108]

notes.problem: The Sugata-heart phrase is a compound not established in the glossary; it parallels the buddha-heart terminology at N-C-103.
notes.treatment: Use sublime Sugata heart provisionally, preserving the Ground and distinguishing སྙིང་པོ from the assigned essence for ངོ་བོ.
notes.uncertainty: The exact attachment of sublime could qualify Sugata or heart.
notes.review_action: Review the compound and modifier attachment.

english: To their following retinues and individual disciples of varied lineages, they excellently teach distinct Dharma particulars without confusion, in accord with lineage and faculties. They distinguish the successive particulars of inclination toward the paths of inferior hearers and solitary victors or supreme awakening, and through teaching establish beings in the three awakenings. The great word of their fame and renown resounds like thunder in the ten directions.[^N-C-109]

notes.problem: སྒྲ denotes both renown’s report and literal thunder-sound; mechanical word in the latter compound would distort the image.
notes.treatment: Retain word for the renown report and use thunder as a scoped whole-expression rendering of འབྲུག་སྒྲ.
notes.uncertainty: The word/sound family needs a broader contextual glossary decision.
notes.review_action: Review this compound together with musical-instrument and mantra-sound uses in the range.

english: Thus the subject matter, the evenness of the Dharma teachings, is profound like honey of a single taste. The enlightened intent of the vast, unsurpassed sūtras, tantras, and treatises that express it is immense like a great ocean. I have spoken only a drop of water taken from that ocean on a hair’s tip. I, Sherab Jungné, a wandering monk living on alms, wrote this.[^N-C-110]

notes.problem: The phrase ཆོས་ཐུན is unusual; the long chain contrasts subject matter with expressive texts and their enlightened intent. Sherab Jungné’s authorial statement precedes the later compiler’s colophon.
notes.treatment: Read Dharma teachings provisionally and preserve the expressed/expressing relationship; classify this as the embedded author’s work colophon.
notes.uncertainty: The ཐུན reading and attachment need checking.
notes.review_action: Collate U04471 and retain the distinction between root author and compiler.

english: Through this virtue, white as a snow mountain and completely pure in the nonfinding of any phenomenon of dedication—who dedicates, to what, and in what way, within the three spheres—may the precious teaching of the victorious ones spread without limit throughout the ten directions to the furthest future. Through its power, may [beings] become completely free from unknowing bewilderment, the root of worldly saṃsāra, and from adventitious stains; may they swiftly attain consummate buddhahood, the very character of the three embodiments and five primordial knowings.[^N-C-111]

notes.problem: The three spheres and dedication grammar are compressed; the beneficiaries of the final aspiration are implicit.
notes.treatment: Render the source’s who/to what/how relations without imposing another threefold list; supply [beings] from the surrounding altruistic context.
notes.review_action: Confirm the dedication’s agents, objects, and beneficiaries.

english: That root text composed by Sherab Jungné was arranged in verse by the Drigung throne-holder, Venerable Könchok Rinchen Trinlé Namgyal Pal Zangpo. It was then rearranged into a continuous sequence together with the supplements and explained through annotations, taking as its basis the scattered notes compiled by the former great and noble one, Paljor Rinpoche, a Śākya monk learned in the ten fields of knowledge.[^N-C-112]

notes.problem: The colophon’s nested agents must be distinguished. Ten qualifies fields of knowledge, not former great beings. The names have irregular spellings.
notes.treatment: Assign versification to the throne-holder, notes to Paljor Rinpoche, and subsequent compilation to the named Togden in the next pair; render names provisionally.
notes.uncertainty: The exact name forms and scope of the continuous-sequence clause need witness verification.
notes.review_action: Check the colophon modifier chain and proper names without transferring the predecessors’ qualities to the compiler.

english: I, the degenerate age’s mendicant, the Drigung incarnation Togden Könchok Thubten Tenpé Gyaltsen, wrote this at Gang Ngön Tashi Chödzong in Mangyül Ladakh, in the female earth-bird year “endowed with four elements,” in the first autumn month according to the Kālacakra, medical, and Chinese reckoning, and the final summer month, Drozhing, according to Indian stellar reckoning, on the thirteenth day of the waning moon. May virtue and goodness increase![^N-C-113]

notes.problem: The calendrical systems and four-elements descriptor are compressed; གྲོ་ཞིན is an unverified month name. No sexagenary cycle is stated.
notes.treatment: Retain female earth-bird, four elements, both seasonal datings, Drozhing, waning phase, and day thirteen; give no Gregorian conversion.
notes.uncertainty: The calendar grouping, month spelling, place name, and absolute year remain unverified.
notes.review_action: Check the colophon witness and calendars before dating the composition absolutely.
